newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks seen getting lift from Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks seen getting lift from Holocaust fund.

text.p: Swiss banks could get a psychological boost from their plan to help set up a Holocaust memorial fund, clearing away a cloud of negative scrutiny that has helped weigh on their shares, analysts said on Friday.

Share prices for the big three Swiss banks -- Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Credit Suisse Group (CS), and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) -- have lagged both the broader Swiss market and the prices of other banks in Europe.

At the heart of the matter, analysts say, is a weak domestic business environment, seven years of economic stagnation in Switzerland, staggering levels of provisions, and restructuring plans last year aimed at improving profitability.

But more recently, the long-running controversy over Swiss bankrolling of Nazi Germany and Jewish groups' charges that Swiss banks hoarded assets of Holocaust victims and their heirs have kept the banks under the spotlight.

"In absolute terms Swiss bank shares rose 12 percent in the last 12 months," far below rates of up to 30 percent in Germany and Britain, said James Alexander, bank analyst at Kleinworth Benson in London.
"I think people are concerned about the quality of earnings. A large part comes from investment banking and this is a volatile area," Alexander said.
But the row over Holocaust accounts and Jewish threats -- now dropped -- to call a boycott of Swiss banks has also played a role in the market.
"This story has had an effect on bank share prices...no one really knows how much of an impact all this could have," said Zurich Kantonalbank analyst Christoph Bieri.
"There certainly is a loss of image in international business and that could have an impact on many areas, although one cannot quantify this," he added.
Bieri pointed out that the matter is far from being settled despite big banks' backing in principle for creating a Holocaust fund alongside the government and other businesses.
"Something else is constantly being dug up and there is the risk that this latest agreement just won't help," he said.

The bigger issue dominating share price developments is whether the banks' considerable provisioning in recent years has been enough and if other restructing in the domestic sector will reduce domestic costs sufficiently.
Alexander has rated only UBS as a buy, based on the view that the bank has been much more thorough with its provisioning and that it is better capitalised than the other two big banks.

He has a long-term buy on Credit Suisse Group, but maintains a wait-and-see attitude toward the group's ambitious medium-term goals of reducing costs by some 700 million Swiss francs ($491 million) and realising long-term revenue enhancements.

He rates SBC as a sell, based on the belief that the bank's provisioning has been insufficient and that its investment banking activities are the weakest among the big three because of a lack of strength in the U.S. market.
Bieri at Kantonalbank said he raised UBS to a "buy" from "hold" today because the share is undervalued.
He's had a "buy" on SBC since June, but keeps a "hold" on Credit Suisse because high expectations about the group's restructuring programme may have added too much to the stock price recently.
